newsitem.title: USA: US junk bond funds get $388.6 mln in new cash - AMG.
newsitem.headline: US junk bond funds get $388.6 mln in new cash - AMG.

text.p: Net cash inflows into U.S. high-yield bond mutual funds were $388.6 million in the latest recorded week which ended July 9, according to AMG Data Services.
This week's number represents the sixth consecutive week of net positive cash flows from mutual funds into the junk bond market.
In the prior two weeks, inflows totalled $182.1 million and $75.9 million, respectively, according to AMG.
Almost $2 billion of new cash has poured into junk bond mutual funds since the beginning of June, according to the data.
Mutual funds cash flows are closely watched by junk bond players because the high-yield bond market has one of the heaviest concentrations of mutual fund money of any major asset class in the U.S.
Analysts estimate anywhere from 25-40 percent of all outstanding junk bonds are held by mutual funds.
AMG's information is tallied from high-yield bond funds that report on a weekly basis. AMG excludes reinvested distributions, therefore representing only net new money coming into a fund.
AMG, based in Arcata, Calif., compiles information on U.S. mutual funds.
